key_insight: Augmenting RL rewards with a rollout-level uniqueness bonus prevents policies from collapsing to a few dominant reasoning patterns, enabling LLMs to discover rarer, creative solutions and improving set-level metrics like pass@k without sacrificing single-trial quality.
problem_solved: Exploration collapse during RL fine-tuning of LLMs: policies concentrate on a small set of high-probability reasoning patterns (raising pass@1) but reduce rollout diversity and hurt pass@k and creative problem solving.
method: Uniqueness-aware reward: augment the standard task reward with a rarity/novelty bonus computed over model rollouts so that infrequently seen solutions receive extra credit.
Set-level regularization: evaluate diversity across generated solution sets (batch- or rollout-level) instead of only regularizing token-level behavior, preventing premature mode collapse.
Adaptive rarity estimation: compute online rarity/similarity scores (e.g., inverse-frequency or similarity-based measures) and balance task quality vs. uniqueness during RL updates.
impact: This approach helps LLMs explore a wider range of valid reasoning paths, improving performance on tasks that benefit from multiple distinct solutions (e.g., code generation, math, creative tasks) and offering practitioners a practical way to trade off quality and diversity during RL tuning.
visual_elements: Before vs After schematic: many identical rollouts (exploration collapse) vs many diverse rollouts (uniqueness-aware RL).
Reward composition diagram: task reward + uniqueness bonus → augmented reward used by RL.
Bar/line chart: pass@k (and pass@1) comparison between baseline RL and uniqueness-aware RL showing diversity gains.
Pipeline flowchart: sampling rollouts → rarity scoring → reward augmentation → RL update.
paper_title: Rewarding the Rare: Uniqueness-Aware RL for Creative Problem Solving in LLMs
paper_authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Yucheng Wang, Yufei He, Jiaying Wu, Yilun Zhao
